baseline: 47/10,000 homelessness in 2021; priority allocation mean wait 17.2 months in 2024–25
affected_populations: Low-income renters, people without secure homes, Aboriginal households, people leaving violence; household-type and location splits needed
severity: Health/safety, displacement and exclusion; potential unequal access to jobs and services
victorian_jurisdiction: State housing services, tenancy settings and planning; Commonwealth income/tax/funding and local planning roles
neutral_question: Which feasible responses most improve sustained safe and affordable housing for low-income Victorians over 12–24 months?
limits_and_competing_interpretation: Rank broad need; first batch narrows to preventing tenancy loss; no claim that supply or subsidies alone solve it

baseline: 102,674 recorded family incidents, year to March 2026, down 3.4%
affected_populations: Victim-survivors and children; women, Aboriginal people and underserved cohorts require disaggregation
severity: Serious injury, fear and loss of safety; recorded incidents cannot count unique victims
victorian_jurisdiction: State prevention, protection, justice and services; Commonwealth welfare and national prevention interact
neutral_question: Which responses reduce repeat violence and improve survivor-defined safety, including harms and unequal access?
limits_and_competing_interpretation: June release identified but not extracted; lower recorded incidents do not establish lower underlying violence

affected_populations: Older people, outdoor workers, poor-quality housing residents and exposed regional communities: distributional hypotheses to test
severity: Potential mortality, illness and livelihood/property loss; exposed population and attributable burden not estimated
victorian_jurisdiction: State adaptation, emergency response, health and emissions-related functions; global mitigation shared
neutral_question: Which state-feasible changes reduce heat/disaster morbidity and exposure most equitably under plausible climate scenarios?
limits_and_competing_interpretation: Statewide exposure does not mean equal harm; climate and biodiversity overlap without additive totals

baseline: Persistent ED four-hour and mental-health-bed eight-hour target misses, 2020–21 to 2024–25
affected_populations: People needing urgent/planned care; clinical urgency, regionality, disability and deprivation splits needed
severity: Potential preventable deterioration; proxy target misses do not quantify attributable deaths
victorian_jurisdiction: State public hospitals and ambulance services; primary care, aged care and funding shared
neutral_question: Which changes reduce clinically harmful delay and improve patient outcomes and access at feasible workforce/cost levels?
limits_and_competing_interpretation: Patient baseline percentage missing; current VAHI page blocked; do not treat targets as optimal outcomes

problem: Loss of native ecosystem condition and resilience
baseline: Native vegetation indicator B:33 poor/deteriorating, high confidence, SoE 2023
affected_populations: State ecosystems and future generations; Traditional Owners, rural communities and landholder distribution require participation
severity: Potential irreversible loss; biodiversity has intrinsic as well as instrumental value
victorian_jurisdiction: State land/water/environment management; private landholders, Traditional Owners and federal protections interact
neutral_question: Which actions measurably improve native habitat condition and persistence per resource used, including trade-offs?
limits_and_competing_interpretation: Scale and harm use ecological rather than person counts; ecological value weight requires human deliberation

problem: Unequal justice-system exposure and repeat harm
baseline: 915 Aboriginal adults in custody June 2025; age-standardised rate 1,636/100,000
affected_populations: Aboriginal people in custody, families, victims and affected communities; adult/youth distinctions essential
severity: Liberty, health and victim safety; custody stocks do not establish unnecessary detention
victorian_jurisdiction: State policing, courts, corrections and diversion; Commonwealth offences/services also relevant
neutral_question: Which approaches reduce repeat victimisation and avoidable custody while maintaining safety, fairness and Aboriginal self-determination?
limits_and_competing_interpretation: Do not divide age-standardised Aboriginal rate by crude all-population rate or equate disparity with one cause

problem: Inability to afford essential food and adequate home conditions
baseline: 2024 food item: 38.7% Aboriginal adults; 12.8% non-Aboriginal adults
affected_populations: Low-income households; Aboriginal adults show marked disparity; household structure and geography need investigation
severity: Material deprivation and impaired wellbeing; avoid combining overlapping hardship counts
victorian_jurisdiction: State concessions, community services and housing quality; Commonwealth income support and national markets central
neutral_question: Which responses reduce material deprivation and improve adequate food and home conditions at sustainable household/public cost?
limits_and_competing_interpretation: Food data do not measure all essentials; national household measure is distinct; thermal trial is not a prevalence estimate

problem: Suicide, distress and unmet mental-health support
affected_populations: People in distress, families and carers; age, sex, First Nations and regional rates needed
severity: Deaths and disability; sentinel mortality does not measure all unmet need
victorian_jurisdiction: State specialist/community care and prevention; Commonwealth primary care and income support shared
neutral_question: Which combinations improve timely support, wellbeing and suicide-related outcomes without increasing coercion or inequity?
limits_and_competing_interpretation: Scale score uncertain: mortality is a narrow sentinel; do not infer a service-caused trend

problem: Exclusion from useful and accessible transport
baseline: 18% of tram services accessible in 2023–24 versus 15% in 2018–19
affected_populations: People with disability or mobility restrictions; outer-suburban/regional non-drivers not measured by tram baseline
severity: Reduced access to care, work and social life; trip-level exclusion unmeasured
victorian_jurisdiction: State service planning and infrastructure; local street access and federal disability framework interact
neutral_question: Which combinations improve completed accessible trips and access to essential destinations for underserved people?
limits_and_competing_interpretation: Tram measure anchors only one part; do not substitute stop/fleet counts for end-to-end access

baseline: On track across five AEDC domains: 53.8% in 2024 versus 57.2% in 2021
affected_populations: Children at school entry; socioeconomic, language, Aboriginal and rural splits need extraction
severity: Persistent developmental disadvantage is a research hypothesis; no individual causal prognosis inferred
victorian_jurisdiction: State early childhood and school services; Commonwealth childcare and family income shared
neutral_question: Which supports improve child wellbeing and developmental opportunity and narrow disparities without stigmatising children?
limits_and_competing_interpretation: Victoria remains above national on-track result; developmental monitoring is not a diagnosis

problem: Preventable road deaths and serious injury
baseline: 291 deaths, 4.1 per 100,000, 2025; above ten-year count average
affected_populations: Unprotected road users; rural exposure and occupation need denominator-based analysis
severity: Death and disabling injury; travel access and enforcement equity trade-offs
victorian_jurisdiction: State road design, speed settings, licensing and enforcement; local roads and Commonwealth funding interact
neutral_question: Which changes reduce deaths and serious injuries per trip while preserving equitable access and mobility?
limits_and_competing_interpretation: Below national fatality rate; serious injury and travel-exposure series missing
